Every leaf is a tiny factory. Plants take in sunlight, water and carbon dioxide, and turn them into sugar and oxygen. This process is called photosynthesis, and almost every living thing on Earth depends on it.

It happens inside small green structures called chloroplasts. They are full of a pigment called chlorophyll, which absorbs red and blue light and reflects green light. That is why most plants look green to us.

The first step needs light. Chlorophyll captures energy from sunlight and uses it to split water molecules. The oxygen from the water is released into the air, which is where most of the oxygen we breathe comes from.

The second step can happen without light. The plant uses the captured energy to pull carbon dioxide out of the air and build it into glucose, a simple sugar. Glucose feeds the plant and becomes the wood, leaves and fruit we see.

Photosynthesis is also a huge part of the climate story. Forests and ocean algae absorb billions of tonnes of carbon dioxide every year. Protecting them is one of the simplest ways to slow down global warming.

So the next time you walk past a tree, remember that it is quietly turning light into food, and giving you the air you breathe.
